ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a circle with center M. Segment AC is a chord labeled 42. Segment CT is another chord, with point S on CT. A red perpendicular from M to chord AC and a red perpendicular from M to chord CT have matching tick marks, indicating the two perpendicular distances from M to the chords are equal. The right-angle marks show these red segments are perpendicular to their respective chords. Reasoning: In a circle, chords that are equidistant from the center are congruent. Since AC and CT are the same distance from center M, CT = AC = 42. Also, a perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord, so MS bisects CT at S. Therefore SC = CT/2 = 42/2 = 21.
